clue.text: Announced shortened examination to do with post-graduate award

indicators.note: announced means spoken out loud, so the phrase that follows is turned into what it sounds like

parts.note: docked means cut short, as a dog's tail is docked; an oral is a spoken examination, as in a viva

explanation.surface: A cut-down exam somehow linked to a postgraduate qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Announced' signals that DOCKED ORAL, said quickly, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective describing a PhD or similar higher research degree awarded after postgraduate study.

clue.text: Givin' name to waxy substance

definitions.meaning: dubbing someone means giving them a name; with the final g dropped, as in the clue's Givin', it becomes the answer
a greasy preparation rubbed into leather boots to soften and waterproof them

explanation.surface: A dropped-g phrase about naming something, set beside a description of a waxy product.
explanation.walkthrough: The clipped apostrophe in 'Givin'' tells you to clip the synonym the same way: dubbing loses its final g.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubbin is the traditional wax-and-tallow dressing used to treat leather footwear.

clue.text: Appetiser from tin — look — with top removed

parts.note: a tin is a can

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, so the initial letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to gape is to stare, to look open-mouthed

explanation.surface: Someone opens a tin, peers in, and finds an appetiser inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A canapé is a small savoury snack served before a meal, a classic party appetiser.

clue.text: Martians are crazy

definitions.meaning: literally, beings from Mars live somewhere other than Earth
idiomatically, someone out of touch with reality or bonkers is said to be in a world of their own

explanation.surface: A blunt verdict that Martians are mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone dreamy or detached from reality, while literally it is where Martians live.

clue.text: A politician, one giving evidence in court

parts.note: Lib is short for a Liberal politician
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A politician is a witness giving evidence at a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defendant's plea, backed by evidence, of having been somewhere else at the time of the crime.

clue.text: College girl in student group

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: A girl from a college is part of a group of students.
explanation.definitionFit: A class is a set of students taught together.

clue.text: SUVs? For a start criminals deviously steal other cars

indicators.note: for a start tells you to take only the opening letter of the next word
acting deviously means going crookedly, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crooks cunningly stealing other people's vehicles, perhaps big four-by-fours.
explanation.walkthrough: CHELSEA TRACTORS is British slang for large off-roaders driven in wealthy Chelsea, a smart London district, where nobody farms; the question mark marks the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A mocking British nickname for sport utility vehicles used for city school runs rather than off-road driving.

clue.text: OK to get off bus, say, holding hands

indicators.note: holding means the first piece wraps around the second

parts.note: to alight is to get off a vehicle, a bus being one example
L and R, left and right, the two hands

explanation.surface: Is it fine to step off the bus while holding hands?
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean satisfactory or acceptable, as in 'that's fine'.

clue.text: Cuddling Nora sadly, utter a word of farewell

indicators.note: cuddling means holding something close, so these pieces wrap round the other

parts.note: to utter is to say

indicators.note: sadly here means badly, so the letters of the name are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hugging a tearful Nora, someone says goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese for goodbye, used in English as a jokey farewell.

clue.text: Family's not circling round entrance to Greater London borough

indicators.note: circling means surrounding, so the family piece goes around the next letter

parts.note: kin means family, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter
turned round means the word not is read backwards

explanation.surface: A family refusing to drive round the way into a Greater London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greater' looks like part of the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingston upon Thames is a borough in south-west Greater London.

clue.text: Asian girl visiting African country, avoiding furthest part

indicators.note: visiting means going into, so the girl goes inside the country's name
the furthest part of a word is its last letter, which is left off

parts.note: Benin is a country in West Africa
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: An Asian girl visits an African country but skips its remotest region.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a person from Bengal, in Bangladesh and eastern India.

clue.text: In a perfect world, I would start to embrace mate

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

parts.note: a mate or friend is an ally

explanation.surface: In an ideal world, someone would begin by hugging their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe how things would be under the best possible circumstances.

clue.text: I'm turning out to be getting better

parts.note: taken as written, minus the apostrophe
proving means turning out to be, as in proving difficult

explanation.surface: Someone announces that they are on the mend.
explanation.definitionFit: Improving means becoming better, recovering or making progress.

clue.text: Child care originally introduced in Israel

indicators.note: introduced in means the letter is put inside the other piece

parts.note: Sion, a variant of Zion, stands for Israel or the Jewish homeland

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A new childcare scheme brought in in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant or offspring, especially of a notable family.

clue.text: School principal right to pursue source of trouble, around half term

indicators.note: to pursue means to come after, so this letter goes at the end
around means the trouble wraps round the next piece

parts.note: a headache is a nuisance or source of trouble

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is chased round school halfway through term.
explanation.definitionFit: The head teacher is the person in charge of a school, its principal.

clue.text: A lady drinking endless salt water

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the lady wraps round the shortened word

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A woman drinks salt water without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt water' reads as one phrase, but 'water' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old name for plain drinking water, the only drink available to the first man in Eden.

clue.text: We'll join crew member leaving European capital, bound for America?

indicators.note: join means the two pieces are put side by side
leaving means the following letter departs from the crew member

parts.note: a steward is a member of a ship's or plane's crew

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A flight attendant leaves a European capital heading for the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European capital' suggests a city, but it is only the letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: From Europe, America lies to the west, so travelling there means heading in that direction; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Picks quarrel with boy eating pastries

indicators.note: eating means taking in, so the boy wraps round the pastries

parts.note: a son is a boy
tarts are pastries

explanation.surface: A boy eating pastries picks a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: To start on someone is to begin attacking or nagging them, to pick a quarrel.

clue.text: Internet era ruined comic, perhaps

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A comedian's career was ruined by the internet age.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic or comedian is one example of a performer who amuses an audience.

clue.text: Hold it up — it's not so big

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the words are read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to rein in is to hold back, so rein means hold

explanation.surface: Someone asks for something to be held up because it is too small.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinier is the comparative of tiny, meaning smaller.

clue.text: Popular nurse's plan

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: A well-liked nurse's scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to mean or aim to do it.

clue.text: Mountainous area recalled in Malory Towers

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountain region is remembered in an Enid Blyton school story.
explanation.walkthrough: Malory Towers is Enid Blyton's series of British boarding-school novels; 'in' signals the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region of western Austria and northern Italy.

clue.text: Supporter wildly chants 1-0: it's the end for London…

indicators.note: wildly means in a disordered way, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 1 is the letter I by its shape and 0 is the letter O

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A football fan chants after a 1-0 defeat for a London side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter' suggests a fan, but it is a post that holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanchion is an upright bar or post that supports a structure.

clue.text: Proverb from the Christian era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the Christian era of dating
an age is an era

explanation.surface: A proverb dating from the Christian era.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a traditional saying or maxim.

clue.text: … team that's left after arena's erupted

indicators.note: after means this letter follows the anagram
erupted means burst apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the London team left after the stadium exploded.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a north London football club, so it is one example of a team.

clue.text: Plant: it is hidden by part of a pine?

indicators.note: is hidden by means the word it goes inside the cone

parts.note: a cone is a part of a pine tree, so part of a pine is a cone

explanation.surface: A plant is concealed by part of a pine tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, is a poisonous flowering plant.

clue.text: Make fruit cake

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a drawing
a nut is a dry fruit

explanation.surface: A command to bake a fruit cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit cake' reads as one thing, and a fruitcake is also a nut, but 'cake' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut, spelt donut in America, is a small fried sweet cake.

clue.text: Leisurely drink safe for consumption

indicators.note: for consumption means taken in, so the drink swallows the next word

parts.note: mead is a drink made from honey
sure means safe, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: A slowly sipped drink that is fit to consume.
explanation.definitionFit: Measured means slow and deliberate, unhurried in pace.
